evals.prompt: I need the Gherkin scenarios for this story: As a customer, I want to recover my password by email so I can get back into my account. Criteria: I receive an email with a link to reset the password; the link expires; the new password must follow the password policy; if the email is not registered, I must not be able to find that out.
evals.expected_output: Analysis separating explicit rules, derivable rules, and points to investigate (expiration period and password policy not defined); variants explored (expired link, already used link, unregistered email, password outside the policy); declarative first-person scenarios; questions about expiration period and password policy, without inventing values.
assertions: Does not invent the link expiration period or the password policy criteria
Records the expiration period and password policy as doubts for the Three Amigos
User actions appear in the When, never in the Given
Scenarios in the first person and without mention of buttons, fields, or URLs
Covers expired link and unregistered email as exceptions
Output in pure Markdown, without code blocks

evals.prompt: Ticket: 'Develop the transfer screen between accounts. The user enters the destination account and the amount and clicks Transfer. Validate balance.' Write the scenarios for me.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that the ticket is technical and vague; extracts the business rule behind it (transfer only with sufficient balance); lists many gaps (limit per transaction, time windows, nonexistent account, same account holder, fees, amount equal to the balance); writes a few safe scenarios and moves the rest to questions.
assertions: Ignores the screen mechanism (clicking Transfer) and writes at the business level
Does not assert behavior for an amount exactly equal to the balance without a defined rule
Lists at least four relevant gaps as questions
Scenarios for sufficient balance and insufficient balance are present

evals.prompt: Free shipping rule: orders above R$ 150 to the South and Southeast regions get free shipping, except bulky products. Premium customers get free shipping in any region starting at R$ 100. Write the specification by example.
evals.expected_output: Applies a decision table (amount, region, bulky, Premium) and boundary values; identifies ambiguities (does 'above' include exactly R$ 150? does 'except bulky' apply to Premium? does the order total include the bulky item?); uses Scenario Outline when there are several rows of the same behavior; discards redundant combinations with justification.
assertions: Identifies the ambiguity of 'above' at the R$ 150 limit and treats it as a question
Identifies the doubt about bulky products for a Premium customer
Uses a decision table or examples outline in a lean way
Does not invent a rule for the North, Northeast, and Center-West regions for non-Premium customers
Records discarded variants with the reason
